pages.text: Dad was going to the market. "I'll be back soon. Look after the inn." Kota was left alone in the yard.
An unfamiliar elderly heron stood at the gate. "Could I stay the night here?" Kota's heart thumped. Dad wasn't here! What could they do?
The heron's legs trembled. She had walked a long, long way. Kota took one big breath. "I'll... give it a try."
Kota brought their paws together, smiled, and bowed. "Welcome to Kota's Inn!" The heron's face lit up. "What a lovely greeting!"
Kota set her shoes on the stepping stone with the toes facing outward. In her room, they flapped the quilt up and spread it flat. "Does the little innkeeper do everything?" she asked, wide-eyed.
"I'll show you the bath! Gentle steam means warm water." She dipped a fingertip and nodded. Along the hallway, they tiptoed and whispered together.
Dad returned that evening, astonished. Shoes side by side, quilt smooth, heron snug in the warm bath. "Kota did... all this?" Kota's tail shot up.
"Thanks to your little innkeeper, my legs feel much better." Dad lifted Kota high. Kota beamed down at the yard.
The next morning, the heron turned at the gate. "I'll come back to Kota's Inn next time." Kota waved both arms high and wide. "See you again!"
That night, Dad hugged Kota on his lap. "Guests you welcome remember you and come again." "Welcome to Kota's Inn tomorrow, too!" Kota was already waiting for the next guest.
